title: Compatibility shim and phased deprecation plan for legacy query endpoints
creator: Anika Sharma
description: Provide a clear, low-risk migration path for customers using legacy query and completions-style endpoints by introducing a server-side compatibility shim, coordinated SDK adapters, targeted telemetry, and a two-phase sunset schedule. The goal is to preserve customer uptime and model quality while removing technical debt and consolidating routing to the structured chat/generate API within 9 months.
background: Over the last 3 years we accumulated multiple legacy endpoints and header-based version flags that overlap in functionality (legacy-query, v0 completions, and free-form generate). This has led to support burden, inconsistent behavior across SDKs, and reduced ability to optimize runtime kernels and batching. Customers have requested longer migration windows and automated tooling. This initiative balances operational simplicity for Redwood with a safe migration experience for customers.
scope: IN SCOPE: 1) Server-side compatibility shim that translates legacy request shapes to the new structured generate/chat API; 2) SDK adapters for JavaScript/Python/Go that surface deprecation warnings and offer an 'auto-migrate' adapter; 3) Console deprecation banners, docs and step-by-step migration playbook; 4) Telemetry and dashboards to track adapter adoption and errors; 5) A two-phase deprecation schedule (announce -> maintain shim -> sunset).
out_of_scope: Direct changes to Dedicated/private control planes (customers on dedicated/private will be handled via separate plan), runtime kernel rewrites, and model architecture changes. Long-term removal of model variants is tracked in a separate initiative.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery): final inventory of legacy endpoints and client distribution (2 weeks). Phase 1 (Shim + Telemetry): implement compatibility shim behind a feature flag that maps payloads and headers to structured generate requests; add error/latency tagging (6 weeks). Phase 2 (SDK adapters): release SDKs with deprecation warnings and opt-in 'auto-migrate' adapter that rewrites client calls client-side (4 weeks). Phase 3 (Beta communications): notify customers, publish migration playbook, enable console banners and in-app warnings (2 weeks). Phase 4 (Stable rollout): gradually enable shim for all customers while monitoring, keep shim for minimum grace period of 6 months after announcement. Phase 5 (Sunset): final remove endpoint after grace period with emergency rollback plan.
rollout_timeline: 2026-04-01: Start Phase 0 inventory. 2026-04-15: Feature-flagged compatibility shim in staging. 2026-05-01: SDK adapter alpha releases (JS/Python). 2026-05-15: Public SDK adapter releases + docs and migration playbook published. 2026-05-20: Official deprecation announcement and console banner begins. 2026-11-20: Target final sunset date for legacy endpoints (6 months grace minimum).
communication_plan: Primary channels: customer dashboard banner, targeted emails to owners of high-usage keys, blog post with migration timeline, in-SDK console warnings, and GitHub issue templates for self-serve. For customers with Dedicated/Private deployments, Solutions Eng will run one-off workshops. Communication cadence: Announcement (T0), Weekly adoption reports to customers and internal stakeholders (T0+1 week onward), Reminder at T0+90 days, Final notice at T0+30 days before sunset.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim accepts >95% of legacy request shapes in integration test suite without functional regression
SDK adapters released for JS/Python/Go with deprecation warning logs and optional auto-migrate flag
Migration playbook and step-by-step docs published in docs.redwood.ai with code samples
Console shows deprecation banner and per-key migration status dashboard
Telemetry dashboard shows adoption metrics (percent calls via shim vs native new API) and error/latency alerts configured
No customer-facing error rate increase >2% attributable to shim within 72 hours of rollout for Tier 1 customers; if exceeded, rollback plan executed
monitoring_and_rollback: Monitor: legacy-route traffic share, adapter adoption rate, error-rate delta, 95th/99th latency, model output drift metrics on sampled prompts, and support ticket volume. Alerts: spike in 5xxs on legacy mapping, model-perplexity/regression alerts, or >5% latency regression. Rollback: flip feature flag to disable shim and route back to original handlers, publish incident postmortem, pause sunset timeline for affected customers, and schedule hotfix release to fix mapping issues.
open_questions: What is the minimum supported SDK version to ship adapters without breaking customers?
Do we require opt-in telemetry consent for older EU customers?
Which legacy models need explicit model_id mapping vs. default routing?
What SLA/credits will we offer if shim-induced regressions impact production customers?
